documents.text: Wherefore, I, Nephi, to be obedient to the commandments of the Lord, went and made these plates upon which I have engraven these things.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 5:31** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Nephi’s flight from angry brothers who seek his life, following the Lord’s warning. Nephi leads his family, Zoram, Sam, Jacob, Joseph, sisters, and believers into the wilderness, settles in a place called Nephi, and forms the people of Nephi who keep the law of Moses and prosper. Nephi makes weapons, teaches crafts, builds a temple, consecrates Jacob and Joseph as priests, describes Lamanites being cut off and cursed, and begins new plates amid later wars."

documents.text: And it came to pass that he had two sons. He gave unto the eldest the name of Nephi, and unto the youngest, the name of Lehi. And they began to grow up unto the Lord.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 3:21** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records contention and dissensions in years 43–48, including migrations from Zarahemla to the land northward, settlement near large waters, cement building, shipping timber, and growth of cities and temples. It notes extensive Nephite recordkeeping and later Nephite decline. Helaman judges with justice, names sons Nephi and Lehi, and peace returns while Gadianton’s secret combinations persist. Many join the church by baptism; later pride brings persecution. Helaman dies; Nephi succeeds.

documents.text: And Nephi, who was the father of Nephi, who had the charge of the records, did not return to the land of Zarahemla, and could nowhere be found in all the land.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 2:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 19 verses and records the people forgetting earlier signs, hardening their hearts, and growing in wickedness as years 95–100 pass, with time reckoned from the sign of Christ’s coming. Nephi, keeper of the records, does not return to Zarahemla and cannot be found. In the thirteenth year wars intensify with numerous Gadianton robbers; converted Lamanites unite with Nephites, are numbered as Nephites, and fight for safety and worship. Fighting continues through years 14–15 with shifting advantages and increasing afflictions.

documents.text: For I, Nephi, was constrained to speak unto them, according to his word; for I had spoken many things unto them, and also my father, before his death; many of which sayings are written upon mine other plates; for a more history part are written upon mine other plates.

Lehi dies and is buried. Laman, Lemuel, and Ishmael’s sons become angry with Nephi. Nephi explains his writing purpose, recounts divine help, angels and visions, and offers prayers for deliverance, strength, and trust in God rather than man.

documents.text: Now this man's name was Nephihah, and he was appointed chief judge; and he sat in the judgment-seat to judge and to govern the people.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 4:17** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records events in the sixth through ninth years of the judges: peace in Zarahemla, mourning and losses from Lamanite destruction, and renewed church growth with baptisms in Sidon led by Alma. It covers rising pride and persecution among church members, resulting contentions and inequality. Alma appoints Nephihah as chief judge and relinquishes the judgment-seat to preach and retain the high priesthood.

documents.text: But I shall make an account of my proceedings in my days. Behold, I make an abridgment of the record of my father, upon plates which I have made with mine own hands; wherefore, after I have abridged the record of my father then will I make an account of mine own life.

This chapter contains 32 verses and records Lehi’s final counsel to his sons in the promised land, recounting deliverance from Jerusalem and sea dangers, and his vision of Jerusalem’s destruction. He prophesies the land is for those led by the Lord and is kept from other nations. He promises prosperity for obedience and warns of cursing, invasion, scattering, and bloodshed for unbelief. He urges repentance, unity, and obedience to Nephi, gives conditional blessings to Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Ishmael’s sons, and blesses Zoram and his descendants.

documents.text: And now it came to pass that there were a great multitude gathered together, of the people of Nephi, round about the temple which was in the land Bountiful; and they were marveling and wondering one with another, and were showing one to another the great and marvelous change which had taken place.

documents.text: And now, my father had begat two sons in the wilderness; the elder was called Jacob and the younger Joseph.

Nephi prays, the storm ceases, and they reach the promised land, plant seeds, and find animals and ores.

query: How many days was Jesus in the tomb?

documents.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 11:17** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture."
**Verse**: "Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already."

documents.text: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
documents.context:

This chapter contains 50 verses and records Jesus defending his disciples’ Sabbath grain picking, healing a man’s withered hand in a synagogue, and Pharisees plotting against him. Jesus heals many and commands silence, with an Isaiah citation. He casts out a demon from a blind, mute man, answers Beelzebub accusations, warns about blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, teaches about words and fruit, refuses a sign except Jonah, describes returning unclean spirits, and identifies doers of God’s will as family."
**Verse**: "For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth."

query: What is the Word of Wisdom?

documents.text: A WORD OF WISDOM, for the benefit of the council of high priests, assembled in Kirtland, and the church, and also the saints in Zion—
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 89:1** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records the Word of Wisdom given in Kirtland for the church, offered as a principle with promise. It warns against wine and strong drink (except sacramental pure wine), limits strong drink to washing, prohibits tobacco and hot drinks, and counsels use of herbs, fruits, grains, and sparing use of meat. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Limhi having Ammon report events since Zeniff and repeat Benjamin’s teachings. Limhi brings the record plates of his people for Ammon to read. Limhi recounts sending 43 men to find Zarahemla; they return with 24 gold plates, breastplates, and rusted swords from a ruined, bone-covered land. Ammon identifies Zarahemla’s king as a seer with interpreters to translate ancient records."

documents.text: "I went to the city of New York, and presented the characters which had been translated, with the translation thereof, to Professor Charles Anthon, a gentleman celebrated for his literary attainments. Professor Anthon stated that the translation was correct, more so than any he had before seen translated from the Egyptian. I then showed him those which were not yet translated, and he said that they were Egyptian, Chaldaic, Assyriac, and Arabic; and he said they were true characters. He gave me a certificate, certifying to the people of Palmyra that they were true characters, and that the translation of such of them as had been translated was also correct. I took the certificate and put it into my pocket, and was just leaving the house, when Mr. Anthon called me back, and asked me how the young man found out that there were gold plates in the place where he found them. I answered that an angel of God had revealed it unto him.

documents.text: The excitement, however, still continued, and rumor with her thousand tongues was all the time employed in circulating falsehoods about my father's family, and about myself. **Context**: "The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:20** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling."
**Verse**: "For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us unto the LORD our God; and according unto all that the LORD our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it."

documents.text: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ephesians 6:18** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 24 verses and covers instructions for children to obey parents and for fathers to nurture without provoking; servants to obey masters sincerely and masters to forbear threatening. It urges believers to be strong, put on the whole armor of God against spiritual powers, and pray continually. Paul requests prayer for bold gospel speech as an imprisoned ambassador, sends Tychicus with news, and closes with peace and grace.

query: What does scripture say about repentance?

documents.text: And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Helaman 12:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Mormon’s reflections on human unsteadiness: people prosper, forget God, and require chastening by afflictions, death, famine, and pestilence. It states God’s power to command earth, mountains, waters, and the length of day, and to curse hidden treasures and individuals for iniquity. It declares repentance as the means of salvation and contrasts final outcomes of everlasting life versus damnation."
**Verse**: "And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared."

documents.text: And also the Spirit saith unto me, yea, crieth unto me with a mighty voice, saying: Go forth and say unto this people—Repent, for except ye repent ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of heaven.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Alma 5:51** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 62 verses and records Alma preaching in Zarahemla, recounting his father’s church in Mormon and deliverance from Noah’s people and the Lamanites. He questions the church about remembering captivity, experiencing a change of heart, and being judged by works. He commands repentance, humility, avoiding pride and persecution, caring for the poor, and producing good fruit. Alma testifies by the Spirit of Jesus Christ’s coming and invites all to be baptized."
**Verse**: "And also the Spirit saith unto me, yea, crieth unto me with a mighty voice, saying: Go forth and say unto this people—Repent, for except ye repent ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of heaven."

documents.text: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 3:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Peter and John healing a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful, causing public amazement in Solomon’s porch. Peter attributes the miracle to faith in Jesus Christ, recounts Israel’s rejection of Jesus before Pilate, and testifies of Jesus’ resurrection. He calls for repentance, cites Moses and the prophets, references the Abrahamic covenant, and states that Jesus is sent first to bless Israel by turning people from iniquities.

documents.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 13:3** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jesus teaching that disasters do not prove greater guilt and calling all to repent; he gives the parable of the barren fig tree. In a synagogue on the sabbath he heals a woman bowed eighteen years and answers the ruler. He compares God’s kingdom to mustard seed and leaven, teaches about the narrow gate and exclusion, notes people from all directions entering. Pharisees warn of Herod; Jesus speaks of his mission and laments Jerusalem’s rejection.

documents.text: But if ye will repent and return unto the Lord your God I will turn away mine anger, saith the Lord; yea, thus saith the Lord, blessed are they who will repent and turn unto me, but wo unto him that repenteth not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Corinthians 7:10** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 16 verses and records Paul urging believers to cleanse themselves and pursue holiness, defending his conduct toward the Corinthians. He describes troubles in Macedonia and comfort received through Titus’s arrival and report of their desire, mourning, and zeal. Paul explains his earlier letter caused temporary sorrow leading to repentance, contrasts godly and worldly sorrow, notes their renewed obedience, and expresses joy, comfort, and confidence in them.

documents.text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 3:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing in the Jordan as people confess sins, and warning Pharisees and Sadducees to produce worthy fruit. John describes one coming after him who baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire and brings judgment. Jesus comes from Galilee, is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a heavenly voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son.

documents.text: Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 3:8** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing in the Jordan as people confess sins, and warning Pharisees and Sadducees to produce worthy fruit. John describes one coming after him who baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire and brings judgment. Jesus comes from Galilee, is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a heavenly voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son.

documents.text: But God hath made known unto our fathers that all men must repent.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:50** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joel 2:13** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records an alarm in Zion about the day of the LORD and a great invading army bringing darkness and devastation. It commands repentance with fasting, assembly, and priestly intercession. The LORD promises pity, removal of the northern army, restoration of crops and rains, and renewal after locust loss. It foretells the Spirit poured on all flesh, cosmic signs, and deliverance for those calling on the LORD in Zion and Jerusalem.

documents.text: Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joel 2:12** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records an alarm in Zion about the day of the LORD and a great invading army bringing darkness and devastation. documents.text: And how great is his joy in the soul that repenteth!
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 18:13** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 47 verses and records revelation to Oliver Cowdery and David Whitmer affirming the truth of their writings and commanding reliance on what is written to found Christ’s church. It commands repentance, faith, hope, and charity; taking upon Christ’s name; and baptism with enduring to the end. It discusses the worth of souls, Christ’s suffering and resurrection, and calls for selecting Twelve disciples to preach, baptize, and ordain priests and teachers.

documents.text: But as oft as they repented and sought forgiveness, with real intent, they were forgiven.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 6:8** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records requirements for baptism: repentance, broken heart, contrite spirit, and taking upon oneself the name of Christ with determination to serve. It describes members being numbered, names recorded, and being nourished by God’s word, prayer, and reliance on Christ. The church meets often to fast, pray, converse, and partake of bread and wine. It outlines discipline for iniquity, removal from records, forgiveness upon repentance, and Spirit-led meetings.

documents.text: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 8:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records persecution after Stephen’s death, with believers scattered from Jerusalem while Saul imprisons many. Philip preaches in Samaria, performs healings and exorcisms, and many are baptized, including Simon the sorcerer. Peter and John confer the Holy Ghost by laying on hands; Simon is rebuked for offering money. Philip later baptizes an Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road and then preaches from Azotus to Caesarea.

documents.text: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Acts 17:18** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Paul and Silas preaching in Thessalonica, some believing, and opposition leading to Jason being accused and released on security. Paul and Silas go to Berea, where many examine Scripture and believe, but Thessalonian Jews stir trouble. Paul is sent to Athens, disputes in synagogue and marketplace, and speaks at the Areopagus about the Creator, repentance, and resurrection; some mock, others believe, including Dionysius and Damaris."
**Verse**: "Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection."

documents.text: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 6:12** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 56 verses and records Jesus teaching in his hometown synagogue and being rejected, healing a few, and traveling to teach. Jesus sends the twelve out in pairs with instructions, and they preach repentance, cast out demons, and heal. Herod hears of Jesus and the chapter recounts John the Baptist’s imprisonment and beheading. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea, reaches Gennesaret, and heals many who touch him.

documents.text: Yea, the LORD will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen:

documents.text: And him that repenteth not of his sins, and confesseth them not, ye shall bring before the church, and do with him as the scripture saith unto you, either by commandment or by revelation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 64:12** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to church elders to overcome the world, repent, and forgive all men, with directions for church discipline of the unrepentant. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

query: What is the role of the Holy Ghost?

documents.text: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Luke 12:12** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 59 verses and records Jesus warning disciples against Pharisaic hypocrisy, urging fear of God, confession of him, and reliance on the Holy Ghost in trials. He refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute, warns against covetousness, and gives the parable of the rich fool. He teaches not to worry, to seek God’s kingdom, give alms, and be watchful like servants. He speaks of accountability, coming division, discerning the times, and reconciling with an adversary before judgment."
**Verse**: "For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say."

documents.text: And the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and the Father giveth the Holy Ghost unto the children of men, because of me.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 28:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records Jesus asking the Nephite disciples what they desire after his departure. Nine request to end their ministry and come to him at age seventy-two; three desire to remain and bring souls to Christ and are promised they will not taste death. They are transfigured, forbidden to reveal what they see, and continue ministering, baptizing, and giving the Holy Ghost. They escape prisons, pits, furnaces, and beasts unharmed; Mormon notes their future ministry among Gentiles, Jews, and Israel and explains their bodily change until judgment."
**Verse**: "And the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and the Father giveth the Holy Ghost unto the children of men, because of me."

documents.text: For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 32:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records Nephi teaching what to do after entering “the way”: receive the Holy Ghost, which enables speaking with the tongue of angels and brings the words of Christ. He commands readers to feast on Christ’s words, ask and knock for understanding, and states this is the doctrine of Christ until Christ manifests in the flesh. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions."
**Verse**: "For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do."

documents.text: Do ye not remember that I said unto you that after ye had received the Holy Ghost ye could speak with the tongue of angels? And now, how could ye speak with the tongue of angels save it were by the Holy Ghost?
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 32:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records Nephi teaching what to do after entering “the way”: receive the Holy Ghost, which enables speaking with the tongue of angels and brings the words of Christ. **Verse**: "Do ye not remember that I said unto you that after ye had received the Holy Ghost ye could speak with the tongue of angels? And now, how could ye speak with the tongue of angels save it were by the Holy Ghost?"

documents.text: Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 32:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions."

documents.text: And this is my gospel—repentance and baptism by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, even the Comforter, which showeth all things, and teacheth the peaceable things of the kingdom.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 39:6** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 24 verses and records Jesus Christ identifying himself and defining his gospel as repentance, water baptism, and baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It addresses James, calls him to be baptized, preach the fulness of the gospel, labor in the vineyard, build the Church, and help bring forth Zion. It directs him to go to Ohio, urges gathering there, calls for missionary labor and repentance, and commands baptism and laying on of hands for the Holy Ghost in preparation for Christ’s coming."
**Verse**: "And this is my gospel—repentance and baptism by water, and then cometh the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, even the Comforter, which showeth all things, and teacheth the peaceable things of the kingdom."

documents.text: And it came to pass when they were all baptized and had come up out of the water, the Holy Ghost did fall upon them, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and with fire.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 19:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 36 verses and records the people gathering again after Jesus ascends, as the twelve chosen disciples teach, organize the multitude, and lead prayer in Jesus’s name. Nephi is baptized and then baptizes the other disciples; the Holy Ghost falls on them with fire, and angels minister. Jesus appears, commands kneeling and prayer, and prays to the Father for the disciples and future believers, noting their great faith."
**Verse**: "And it came to pass when they were all baptized and had come up out of the water, the Holy Ghost did fall upon them, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and with fire."

documents.text: But now I give unto thee a commandment, that thou shalt baptize by water, and they shall receive the Holy Ghost by the laying on of the hands, even as the apostles of old.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 35:6** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records the Lord identifying Himself as Jesus Christ and addressing Sidney Rigdon, calling him to a greater work, commanding him to baptize and confer the Holy Ghost by laying on of hands, and promising signs to believers. It covers preaching the fulness of the gospel through Joseph Smith, keys and revelations, Sidney’s assignment to write for Joseph, exhortations to keep commandments, support Joseph, and promises concerning Zion, Israel, and the Lord’s coming."
**Verse**: "But now I give unto thee a commandment, that thou shalt baptize by water, and they shall receive the Holy Ghost by the laying on of the hands, even as the apostles of old."

documents.text: The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **D&C 130:22** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records teachings about seeing the Savior as a man, continued sociality after this life, and a personal appearing of the Father and Son. It addresses differing reckoning of time by planets, angels ministering only to their own earth, and God’s residence as a Urim and Thummim; the sanctified earth and individual white stones function similarly. It includes prophecy of bloodshed beginning in South Carolina, a statement about Joseph Smith possibly seeing the Son of Man, principles of intelligence gained in mortality, blessings tied to obedience to law, and the embodied nature of the Father and Son versus the Holy Ghost."
**Verse**: "The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us."

documents.text: And again, it shall come to pass that on as many as ye shall baptize with water, ye shall lay your hands, and they shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost, and shall be looking forth for the signs of my coming, and shall know me.

documents.text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 14:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Jesus consoling his disciples, promising to prepare a place in the Father’s house and to return. He answers Thomas about the way to the Father, teaches Philip about seeing the Father through him, and promises believers will do works and have prayers answered in his name. He commands keeping his commandments, promises the Comforter/Holy Ghost, gives peace, foretells his departure, and mentions the prince of this world.

documents.text: Wherefore, I now send upon you another Comforter, even upon you my friends, that it may abide in your hearts, even the Holy Spirit of promise; which other Comforter is the same that I promised unto my disciples, as is recorded in the testimony of John.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 88:3** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 141 verses and records the Lord’s instructions to assembled elders about the Holy Spirit of promise, the light of Christ, resurrection, and laws governing celestial, terrestrial, and telestial kingdoms. It describes earth’s sanctification and cosmic order, gives a parable of laborers, and commands prayer, sanctification, study, and organizing a school and house of God. It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass, that if you shall ask the Father in my name, in faith believing, you shall receive the Holy Ghost, which giveth utterance, that you may stand as a witness of the things of which you shall both hear and see, and also that you may declare repentance unto this generation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 14:8** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord declaring a great work coming forth and urging heed to His word. It calls willing laborers to harvest and promises salvation for enduring and keeping commandments. It commands seeking to establish Zion, asking in faith, and receiving the Holy Ghost to witness and declare repentance. Jesus Christ identifies Himself and states He will bring the fulness of the gospel from the Gentiles to Israel, calling David to assist.

documents.text: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 16:13** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records Jesus warning the disciples of expulsion from synagogues and persecution, explaining his departure to the Father, and promising the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who convicts the world and guides into truth. Jesus speaks of a short time of sorrow turning to joy, instructs prayer to the Father in his name, affirms his origin and return to the Father, predicts the disciples’ scattering, and promises peace amid tribulation.

documents.text: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 15:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Jesus teaching that he is the true vine and disciples must abide in him to bear fruit, with unfruitful branches removed. He commands keeping his commandments and loving one another, calls disciples friends, and says he chooses and ordains them to bear lasting fruit and pray in his name. He warns of the world’s hatred and persecution, explains responsibility for rejecting his words and works, cites “hated without a cause,” and promises the Comforter to testify; disciples also witness.

documents.text: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 20:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Mary Magdalene finding the stone removed and reporting to Peter and the other disciple, who inspect the empty tomb and linen cloths. Mary sees two angels and then Jesus, who tells her to report to the disciples. Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his wounds, commissions them, gives the Holy Ghost, and speaks of remitting or retaining sins. Thomas doubts, then sees Jesus and confesses him. The chapter states the purpose of the written signs.

documents.text: Wherefore, watch over him that his faith fail not, and it shall be given by the Comforter, the Holy Ghost, that knoweth all things.

**Context**: "The following passage is from **Job 26:12** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 14 verses and records Job answering, questioning how his friend has helped the powerless or given true counsel. Job then lists God’s acts of power over creation: forming things under waters, seeing Sheol and destruction, stretching out the heavens and suspending earth, binding waters in clouds, setting bounds for seas and day and night, shaking heaven’s pillars, dividing the sea, and forming the heavens and the crooked serpent."
**Verse**: "He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud."

documents.text: And I, God, called the firmament Heaven; and the evening and the morning were the second day.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 2:8** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records the Lord revealing to Moses the creation of heaven and earth in six days: light and darkness; the firmament and divided waters; dry land, seas, and vegetation; sun, moon, and stars; sea life and birds with a command to multiply; land animals; and the creation of man and woman in God’s image with dominion and provisions of plants for food.

query: What do scriptures say about prophets being rejected?

documents.text: And it came to pass that the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection, for the people sought to destroy them.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Ether 11:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records prophets warning King Com’s people to repent; the people reject them and seek to kill them, so they flee to Com. It recounts reigns and conflicts under Shiblom, Seth, Ahah, Ethem, Moron, and Coriantor, including wars, famine, pestilence, and executions of prophets. Secret combinations fuel rebellions, overthrows, and long captivities. Prophets also foretell utter destruction and another people possessing the land. Coriantor begets Ether."
**Verse**: "And it came to pass that the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection, for the people sought to destroy them."

documents.text: Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Jeremiah 6:30** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records a warning for Benjamin to flee Jerusalem as destruction comes from the north, with siege preparations against Zion. It lists Jerusalem’s oppression, violence, covetousness, and false prophets proclaiming “peace.” The LORD urges seeking the old paths and heeding watchmen, but the people refuse; sacrifices are rejected. A northern nation attacks, bringing fear and mourning; Judah is tested like metal and called rejected silver."
**Verse**: "Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them."

documents.text: For behold, they have rejected the words of the prophets. Wherefore, if my father should dwell in the land after he hath been commanded to flee out of the land, behold, he would also perish. Wherefore, it must needs be that he flee out of the land.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Nephi 3:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Lehi’s dream commanding Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem for Laban’s brass plates containing Jewish records and their genealogy. Nephi agrees; the brothers travel to Jerusalem. Laman’s request is rejected and threatened. They offer their family riches; Laban attempts to kill them and seizes the property. Laman and Lemuel beat Nephi and Sam; an angel commands them to return and promises deliverance."
**Verse**: "For behold, they have rejected the words of the prophets. Wherefore, if my father should dwell in the land after he hath been commanded to flee out of the land, behold, he would also perish. Wherefore, it must needs be that he flee out of the land."

documents.text: For behold, the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. For behold, ye have closed your eyes, and ye have rejected the prophets; and your rulers, and the seers hath he covered because of your iniquity.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Nephi 27:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records prophecies about Gentiles and Jews in the last days, divine judgments, and nations fighting Zion. It describes the coming forth of a sealed book, its delivery to an unlearned man, and the role of three and other witnesses. It notes the learned refuse to read a sealed book, and the Lord commands the sealed portion kept. It covers a “marvelous work,” exposure of secret works, and future restoration where the deaf and blind receive understanding and Jacob’s children sanctify God."
**Verse**: "For behold, the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. For behold, ye have closed your eyes, and ye have rejected the prophets; and your rulers, and the seers hath he covered because of your iniquity."

documents.text: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 4:24** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 44 verses and records Jesus’ forty-day temptation in the wilderness and his Scripture responses. It covers his return to Galilee, teaching in synagogues, and reading Isaiah in Nazareth, declaring its fulfillment, and being rejected and threatened. It describes ministry in Capernaum: casting out an unclean spirit, healing Simon’s mother-in-law and many sick, silencing demons, withdrawing to a desert place, and continuing to preach in Galilee.

documents.text: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 6:4** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 56 verses and records Jesus teaching in his hometown synagogue and being rejected, healing a few, and traveling to teach. Jesus sends the twelve out in pairs with instructions, and they preach repentance, cast out demons, and heal. Herod hears of Jesus and the chapter recounts John the Baptist’s imprisonment and beheading. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea, reaches Gennesaret, and heals many who touch him.

documents.text: Behold ye are worse than they; for as the Lord liveth, if a prophet come among you and declareth unto you the word of the Lord, which testifieth of your sins and iniquities, ye are angry with him, and cast him out and seek all manner of ways to destroy him; yea, you will say that he is a false prophet, and that he is a sinner, and of the devil, because he testifieth that your deeds are evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:26** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Zechariah 13:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records a fountain opened for the house of David and Jerusalem for sin and uncleanness, the cutting off of idols, prophets, and an unclean spirit from the land, and punishment of false prophecy. It mentions prophets denying their role and explaining wounds. The LORD calls for the shepherd to be struck and the sheep scattered; two-thirds die, and a remnant is refined and acknowledged as God’s people.

documents.text: Yea, wo unto this people, because of this time which has arrived, that ye do cast out the prophets, and do mock them, and cast stones at them, and do slay them, and do all manner of iniquity unto them, even as they did of old time.

He explains why he uses parables and interprets the sower and tares to the disciples, including end-of-world separation by angels. He returns to his country, faces offense and unbelief, and does few mighty works.

He laments widespread wickedness, with Gadianton robbers controlling judgment-seats and corruption in government. From a tower in his garden by the highway to the market, he addresses gathered people, commands repentance, warns of scattering, loss of cities and lands, and destruction, and declares the Lord reveals these warnings.

documents.text: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honour in his own country.

The woman testifies, and many Samaritans believe; Jesus stays two days. In Galilee he returns to Cana and heals a nobleman’s son in Capernaum by word.

It outlines blessings for receivers, rejection and foot-cleansing testimony for rejecters, and coming judgment. documents.text: Wherefore, he shall bring forth his words unto them, which words shall judge them at the last day, for they shall be given them for the purpose of convincing them of the true Messiah, who was rejected by them; and unto the convincing of them that they need not look forward any more for a Messiah to come, for there should not any come, save it should be a false Messiah which should deceive the people; for there is save one Messiah spoken of by the prophets, and that Messiah is he who should be rejected of the Jews.

He states the Messiah comes 600 years after Lehi leaves Jerusalem and is Jesus Christ. Nephi teaches salvation through Christ, preservation of the record, grace, and keeping Moses’s law until fulfilled.

documents.text: And a prophet of the Lord have they slain; yea, a chosen man of God, who told them of their wickedness and abominations, and prophesied of many things which are to come, yea, even the coming of Christ.

Limhi describes Lamanite bondage and heavy tribute, recounts Zeniff’s deception, internal contentions, and the killing of a prophet. He calls the people to repent, trust God, and serve him for deliverance.

documents.text: And the Lord will surely prepare a way for his people, unto the fulfilling of the words of Moses, which he spake, saying: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you. He describes the Lord revealing covenants, bringing Israel from captivity, and opposing the great and abominable church. Nephi recounts judgments of fire and conflict, identifies Moses’s prophet as the Holy One of Israel, warns against corrupt churches, and urges repentance, obedience, and enduring.

query: How is the gathering of Israel described across scripture?

documents.text: And it shall come to pass that my people, which are of the house of Israel, shall be gathered home unto the lands of their possessions; and my word also shall be gathered in one. And I will show unto them that fight against my word and against my people, who are of the house of Israel, that I am God, and that I covenanted with Abraham that I would remember his seed forever.

It states God speaks to many nations and commands all peoples to write his words, which will judge the world. It foretells shared records among Jews, Nephites, and lost tribes, and Israel’s gathering."
**Verse**: "And it shall come to pass that my people, which are of the house of Israel, shall be gathered home unto the lands of their possessions; and my word also shall be gathered in one. documents.text: O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you.
documents.context:

This chapter contains 19 verses and records the people’s silence after the voice from heaven, then a renewed voice calls the house of Israel to repent, promising gathering or desolation. It states prophecies are fulfilled, the more righteous are spared, cites Zenos, Zenock, and Jacob, and foreshadows Christ’s manifestation to Nephites and spared Lamanites."
**Verse**: "O ye people of these great cities which have fallen, who are descendants of Jacob, yea, who are of the house of Israel, how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you."

It covers Gentile involvement in gathering Israel, promises about a land of inheritance, liberty without kings, and God’s protection of Zion. Jacob urges repentance, freedom to choose life or death, reconciliation to God, and salvation through grace, resurrection, and atonement.

documents.text: And then will I gather them in from the four quarters of the earth; and then will I fulfil the covenant which the Father hath made unto all the people of the house of Israel.

This chapter contains 20 verses and records Jesus saying he has other sheep elsewhere and will visit them by the Father’s command. He commands the Nephites to write his words to be preserved and manifested to the Gentiles, bringing scattered Israel to knowledge and a gathering. It blesses believing Gentiles, warns unbelieving Gentiles, and states the gospel will return to Israel. It affirms this land as Israel’s inheritance and quotes Isaiah about Zion’s restoration.

It covers an ensign sought by Gentiles, the Lord recovering Israel’s remnant from many lands, gathering Judah, ending Ephraim–Judah envy, subduing neighboring nations, drying waters for passage, and a highway from Assyria.

documents.text: And verily I say unto you, I give unto you a sign, that ye may know the time when these things shall be about to take place—that I shall gather in, from their long dispersion, my people, O house of Israel, and shall establish again among them my Zion;

query: What do scriptures say about caring for the poor?

documents.text: Verily, verily, I say that I would that ye should do alms unto the poor; but take heed that ye do not your alms before men to be seen of them; otherwise ye have no reward of your Father who is in heaven.
documents.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **3 Nephi 13:1** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus’ instructions on giving alms, praying, and fasting in secret rather than for public praise. It gives a model prayer and commands forgiveness of others. It warns against storing earthly treasures, serving God and Mammon, and having an evil eye. Jesus charges the twelve to minister and teaches not to worry about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first."
**Verse**: "Verily, verily, I say that I would that ye should do alms unto the poor; but take heed that ye do not your alms before men to be seen of them; otherwise ye have no reward of your Father who is in heaven."

documents.text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Proverbs 19:17** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 29 verses and covers proverbs contrasting integrity with deceit, and wisdom with haste, anger, and folly. It addresses effects of wealth and poverty on friendships, and warns that false witnesses and liars face punishment. It notes kings’ wrath and favor, family troubles from a foolish son and contentious wife, and the value of a prudent wife. It commands keeping commandments, showing pity to the poor, disciplining children, receiving counsel, avoiding sloth, honoring parents, and warns of judgment for scorners and fools.

documents.text: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.

It mandates freeing Hebrew servants in the seventh year with liberal provisions, with an ear-piercing rite for lifelong service. It also requires dedicating firstborn male herd and flock, eating them at the chosen place, rejecting blemished animals, and forbidding blood consumption.

query: What do scriptures teach about the nature of God?

documents.text: We believe in God, the Eternal Father, and in His Son, Jesus Christ, and in the Holy Ghost.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Articles of Faith 1:1** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.

documents.text: And they are one God, yea, the very Eternal Father of heaven and of earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 15:4** from the **Book of Mormon**. He defines Christ’s “seed” as prophets and believers who heed their words. He quotes Isaiah on publishing peace and salvation. He teaches resurrection, a first resurrection for prophets, the obedient, the ignorant, and little children, and excludes willful rebels. He foresees salvation proclaimed to all nations and Zion/Jerusalem restored.

documents.text: The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us.

It addresses differing reckoning of time by planets, angels ministering only to their own earth, and God’s residence as a Urim and Thummim; the sanctified earth and individual white stones function similarly. It includes prophecy of bloodshed beginning in South Carolina, a statement about Joseph Smith possibly seeing the Son of Man, principles of intelligence gained in mortality, blessings tied to obedience to law, and the embodied nature of the Father and Son versus the Holy Ghost.
